item.title: What we know about war plans that Trump and Netanyahu are drawing up
item.description: Could the U.S. and Israel be on the verge of launching a new attack on Iran? President Trump and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have been suggesting that's on the table.

item.title: The historic significance of the WWII-era globe damaged by Pete Hegseth's staff
item.description: A WWII-era globe – one that once belonged to President Dwight Eisenhower – was damaged after an attempted relocation to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's office.

item.title: Questions swirl around Eagles QB Jalen Hurts and embolism diagnosis
item.description: NPR's Juana Summers talks with Lindsay Jones of The Ringer about Jalen Hurts, quarterback for the Philadelphia Eagles. After his blood clot diagnosis, there are questions about how he's being treated.

item.title: In Baltimore, dirt bikers seek a legal way to ride
item.description: Dirt bike riding has been a part of Baltimore's Black culture for decades. But it creates tensions between riders, residents and the police. In Baltimore, one group is looking for common ground.

item.description: The New York Times reported that the Trump Administration is considering physically moving the White House press corps out of the White House.

item.title: What would Brewers fans trade for World Series tickets? Plumbing and a boat, to start
item.description: What would you trade for the chance to watch your team win its first World Series? For some Milwaukee Brewers fans, the answers include plumbing services, or even a boat.

item.title: Rural voters have soured on Trump. In Ohio, that could decide the Senate election
item.description: There are multiple toss-up races in Ohio, including a high profile contest for U.S. Senate. But if Democrats want to win the seat, they'll have to reach out to traditionally Republican voters.

item.title: Gene editing scientists slowed down for safety. Could AI leaders follow their guide?
item.description: Some of the leaders of the AI race are calling for a slowdown, for safety's sake. Viewed in economics terms, it's a collective action problem: no one wants to slow down unless everyone does.

item.title: Albania's violent anti-government protests escalate
item.description: In the Albanian capital of Tirana, protesters squared off with police in what have become violent daily protests over what they say is a corrupt government.

item.title: A family's fundraising for gene therapy research pays off
item.description: After their daughter was diagnosed with a rare inherited disease in 2013, the O'Neill family raised money to find a treatment. The Food and Drug Administration recently approved a gene therapy.
